previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and liver transplant was admitted with fever and worsening right upper quadrant abdominal pain. She was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics due to concern for infection in the setting of immunosuppression. Blood cultures and imaging showed no evidence of bacterial infection or biliary complications. The fever resolved, and she remained asymptomatic off antibiotics. Her symptoms were determined to be non-infectious, possibly related to underlying inflammation. She improved clinically, with stable lab values and liver function, and was discharged home on her baseline immunosuppressive regimen with instructions to follow up as scheduled.

constipation. The transplant surgery team evaluated you and it 
was deemed that you did not have any appendicitis. Your labs did 
not show any evidence of inflammation of your blood vessels or 
evidence of rheumatologic disease. Your MRCP was reassuringly 
normal. It is unclear what is the source of your abdominal pain, 
however, it may be a result of the coils that were placed during 
your liver transplant. We will continue to monitor this closely 
and continue you on Zofran and pain medications for symptomatic 
management.

If you develop fevers, chills, worsening abdominal pain please 
call your doctor or return to the emergency department.

It was a pleasure taking care of you. We wish you the best in 
your health.

Sincerely,
Your ___ Liver Team

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

   1) Stationary Acquisition 6.0 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 43.3 mGy (Body) DLP =

   2) Spiral Acquisition 4.7 s, 51.0 cm; CTDIvol = 13.6 mGy (Body) DLP = 690.9
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 713 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Same-day Doppler ultrasound stomach Multiple prior CTs, most
recently ___

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST:   Small right nonhemorrhagic pleural effusion with overlying
atelectasis. Visualized lung fields are otherwise within normal limits. No
pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: There are postsurgical changes from split liver transplant. 
Unchanged chronic occlusion of the middle hepatic vein.  There is a portal
vein stent, which appears patent.  The SMV and splenic vein also appear
patent.  The liver parenchyma is heterogeneous, likely perfusional.   There is
no evidence of focal lesions.  Unchanged small volume of perihepatic fluid. 
There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The
gallbladder is surgically absent.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: Splenomegaly, measuring 15.5 cm.  The spleen shows normal attenuation
throughout, without evidence of focal lesions.  Again seen are embolization
coils in the location of the prior splenorenal shunt.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: Again seen are embolization coils from prior gastric
variceal embolization.  The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops
demonstrate normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  The
colon and rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is not visualized,
but there are no secondary signs of appendicitis.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: Fibroid uterus, as before.

LYMPH NODES: Unchanged indeterminate soft tissue density encircling the ___
(___).  There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There is
no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES: Interval decrease in stranding within the midline anterior
abdominal wall, likely postsurgical.

Liver: Status post right hepatic lobe living donor liver transplant.  No

There is no ascites.

There is no perihepatic collection.

Pancreas: Normal in size. Parenchyma is normal in signal and enhancement. Main

Spleen: Splenomegaly.  No lesion.

Vasculature: Aorta is of normal caliber. There is a stent noted within the

Hepatic artery is patent.

Embolization coils are present within varices.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: A few small nodules are noted in the
